discovery: Prediction and experimental realization of topological insulators, including the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects

nominees.name: Qikun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech), Shenzhen, and Tsinghua University, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum materials
motivation: Kane, with Mele, showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new, topologically protected insulating state of matter with conducting edge or surface states, founding the field of topological insulators. Molenkamp turned this into experimental fact: by mastering the epitaxial growth of HgTe/CdTe quantum wells he observed the quantum spin Hall effect in 2007, the first topological insulator. Xue, through atomically controlled molecular-beam epitaxy of magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films, discovered the quantum anomalous Hall effect in 2013, quantized Hall conductance without any external magnetic field, a decades-old prediction. Together these works established topology as an organizing principle of electronic matter, now central to condensed matter physics and to proposals for dissipationless electronics, metrology and topological quantum computing. They also show how precise crystal growth of semiconductor heterostructures and thin films turns deep theoretical ideas into measurable new physics.
